issues.t: Engine dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off without warning, sometimes at highway speed, and the steering and brakes get heavy. It may not restart right away, and there is often no check engine light.
issues.why: No single cause has been confirmed. Owners and shops have found failed crankshaft position sensors, failed cam phasers, a failing TIPM power module and software faults; some cars were helped by a software update.
issues.next: Keep a note of when it happens and ask the dealer to check for software updates and stored codes. Have the crank sensor and power module tested before replacing the engine computer.

issues.t: Integrated power module (TIPM) failure
issues.sym: Wipers stuck on or turning on by themselves, horn or lights acting on their own, cranks but won't start, stalling, or the cooling fan not running.
issues.why: The totally integrated power module (the under-hood fuse and relay box with a built-in circuit board) loses internal connections and sends power to the wrong circuits or none at all.
issues.next: If several unrelated electrical things misbehave, ask the shop to test the TIPM. A new module must be programmed, and parts can take weeks, so order early.

issues.t: Passenger side heater blows cold
issues.sym: Warm air on the driver side but cool or lukewarm air on the passenger side, weak defrosting, and sometimes a coolant smell.
issues.why: The heater core gets partly blocked by sludge and deposits in the coolant, so only part of it gets hot. Flushing rarely fixes it for long.
issues.next: Have the coolant level and condition checked first. If the core is clogged, it has to be replaced, which means taking the dash apart.

issues.t: Clicking or clacking behind the dash
issues.sym: A repeating click or clack from behind the dashboard, often when starting the car or changing climate settings.
issues.why: The small electric motors (actuators) that move the heating and A/C doors lose their position or skip, sometimes because of a software glitch.
issues.next: Ask the shop to run an HVAC actuator recalibration. If the noise keeps coming back, the noisy actuator is replaced.

issues.t: Jerky shifting or slipping (2011-2014)
issues.sym: Jolts or jerks when the car shifts, a slipping feeling with the engine revving, or harsh downshifts when slowing.
issues.why: The four-speed and six-speed automatics in the first-generation 200 can shift harshly from adaptive software problems, worn solenoids or internal wear.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the shop look for software updates and do a quick relearn. Get slipping looked at soon to avoid a full rebuild.

issues.t: Left cylinder head failure and misfires
issues.sym: Check engine light with a misfire (often cylinder 2), rough running and a ticking from the left side of the engine.
issues.why: On early 3.6L Pentastar engines, valve seats in the left cylinder head wear, dropping compression. Chrysler extended the warranty on this head for affected vehicles.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed and ask a Chrysler dealer whether the extended head warranty still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Oil filter housing leak
issues.sym: Oil drips at the back of the engine, a burning oil smell, and sometimes coolant loss.
issues.why: The plastic oil filter housing and oil cooler on the 3.6L V6 crack or leak at the gaskets.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. The housing is replaced as an assembly, often with an updated part.

issues.t: Ticking from worn rocker arms
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the top of the engine, sometimes with a misfire code.
issues.why: Rocker arm roller bearings on the 3.6L V6 wear out and can then damage the camshaft.
issues.next: Have it checked early. Replacing rockers before the cam is damaged costs much less.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving (2015-2017)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while slowing, turning or cruising, sometimes after the dash lights flicker. Restarting may take several tries, and often no code is stored.
issues.why: This is the most-reported problem on the second-generation 200. Loose wiring at the power distribution center, the power module and engine computer are among the causes found; early 2015 cars were recalled for a faulty power distribution connector.
issues.next: Check for open recalls first. Write down when it happens and ask the dealer to inspect the power distribution center connections.

issues.t: Rough, delayed or erratic shifting from the 9-speed automatic
issues.sym: Harsh or late shifts, lurching at low speed, hesitation pulling away, or a Service Transmission message.
issues.why: The nine-speed automatic in the second-generation 200 is known for poor shift quality. Software updates help many cars; some need wiring or control module repairs.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest transmission software and a shift relearn. If it slips or drops out of gear, stop driving and get it checked.

issues.t: Oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, the low oil light comes on, or blue smoke at start-up.
issues.why: The 2.4L Tigershark four-cylinder can burn oil, often from stuck piston rings.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every few fill-ups and keep records. Ask the dealer about an oil consumption test and any software or piston ring updates.

issues.t: Transmission can shift to neutral without warning (recall)
issues.sym: The car drops into neutral while driving and may show Service Transmission.
issues.why: Wiring harness crimps for the 9-speed transmission may be poor, so the transmission loses its signal and goes to neutral.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-529 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Car can roll away in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car moves after being put in Park.
issues.why: The parking pawl in the 9-speed transmission can be contaminated or its rod can break, so Park may not hold.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-090 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Power distribution connector can cause stalling (recall)
issues.sym: Intermittent loss of power and stalling.
issues.why: A faulty connector at the power distribution center can lose contact.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-470 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Driver door wiring can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Burning smell from the driver door or power window and lock problems.
issues.why: The driver door wiring harness may overheat and melt, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-480 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Rear shock absorber can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear and poor handling or braking.
issues.why: A weld on the rear shock absorber may be weak, letting the shock detach.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-392 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor may be mismatched (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light, or the passenger airbag status light acting oddly.
issues.why: If the seat occupant sensor and cushion foam were not replaced as a set, the passenger airbag may deploy wrongly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-114 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Radio software can let hackers reach car systems (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms.
issues.why: A security hole in the Uconnect radio software could let an outsider access vehicle control systems.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-461 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Cruise control may not turn off (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control keeps holding or raising speed after you brake or switch it off.
issues.why: A short circuit in the wiring can stop cruise control from canceling.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-332 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Steering fasteners may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or vague steering, or clunks over bumps.
issues.why: Some chassis fasteners on cars built in late May 2016 were not tightened enough.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-589 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Airbags and seat belt pretensioners may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: The occupant restraint control module can short circuit and stop the front and side airbags and belt pretensioners from working.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-668 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Active head restraints may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms.
issues.why: A part in the restraint control module can fail, so the front active head restraints may not move forward in a rear crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-282 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Steering column rivet may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms; possibly a loose steering column.
issues.why: A pivot rivet in the steering column may be missing or installed wrong, weakening the column in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 11V-315 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearings can fail from debris (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, low oil pressure, or engine seizure.
issues.why: Debris left in some 3.6L engines built in early September 2011 can ruin the rod bearings.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 11V-487 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve can break and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Stalling or a fuel smell.
issues.why: A broken control valve in the fuel tank can stall the engine or leak fuel.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-043 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.

issues.t: Balance shaft debris can cause loss of oil pressure (recall)
issues.sym: Oil pressure warning, engine noise or stalling.
issues.why: Abrasive debris in the balance shaft bearings of some 2.4L engines can lead to loss of oil pressure.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-552 on the NHTSA site or with a Chrysler dealer. The fix is free.
